question: Which of the following food is NOT iron rich?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lemon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lemon** is not considered an iron-rich food. It is mainly known for its high vitamin C content.
 
• Vitamin C in **lemon** helps in the absorption of iron from other foods, particularly plant-based sources.
 
• Unlike spinach, red meat, and peas, **lemon** does not contribute significantly to dietary iron intake.
 
• The primary nutrient in **lemon** is vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iron-Rich Foods**

 
 
• **Spinach:** A leafy green vegetable that is a good source of non-heme iron, especially important for vegetarians.
 
• **Red Meat:** Contains heme iron, which is more easily absorbed by the body compared to non-heme iron found in plant sources.
 
• **Peas:** A legume that provides a moderate amount of non-heme iron, along with protein and fiber.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin C**
 
 
• Vitamin C, also known as ascorbic acid, is essential for the growth, development, and repair of body tissues.
 
• It helps in the absorption of non-heme iron from plant-based foods, which can help prevent iron deficiency anemia.
 
• Foods rich in vitamin C include citrus fruits like lemons, oranges, and grapefruits, as well as strawberries, bell peppers, and broccoli.
 
• Regular consumption of vitamin C-rich foods can enhance the body's ability to absorb iron from plant sources, making them crucial for individuals on a vegetarian or vegan diet.
 
 
 
• **Iron Absorption**
 
 
• Iron absorption can be affected by several factors including the form of iron (heme vs non-heme), the presence of enhancers (like vitamin C), and inhibitors (like calcium and certain polyphenols).
 
• Heme iron, found in animal products like red meat, is generally absorbed more efficiently by the body compared to non-heme iron found in plant-based foods.
 
• Consuming vitamin C-rich foods along with iron-rich plant foods can significantly improve the absorption of non-heme iron.
